title: The Best Photoshop Alternative is Now Free

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
Affinity Photo was the best subscription free Photoshop alternative on the market. Unfortunately, buying the entire suite was out of many people's price range. It looked like Affinity was about headed to a subscription based model; something most of the customers were dreading. The CEO announced today the big secret is that Affinity Design, Page, and Photo were being integrated together into one app that users can control. Additionally, all of the key functionality will be free for everyone. Since not all audiences have agreed to AI, there is a premium subscription for adding AI into your workflow with the model. For those looking to distinguish their automated work and handmade work, your solution is here.
You can get your copy of
Affinity for free here
.

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
Dark_Ansem said:
Is it actually the best alternative?
Click to expand...
My top free alternatives:
BeFunky
Dragon Bones: Yanfly/VisuStella made an interesting plugin for Dragon Bones that improves animation.
Gimp
Inkscape
Krita
Paint .Net
Pixlr
Photoshop Express: Photoshop Express is exactly like Photoshop except it is a lite version without any bells & whistles.
Pro Motion NG: Pro Motion improves animation for keyframing.
Pyxel Edit
Affinity combined Adobe Illustrator, Pagemaker, and Photoshop together into one app. It lets you customize it as simple or as complex as you want. No more memorizing file types per use, one file type.  It does have export options for other people. Krita has a similar file type philosophy.
This was my workflow for RPG Maker. I would make a painting in Illustrator, import into Photoshop to create the keyframes, import that into Spriter to smooth the animation, then export the sprites into RPG Maker.
It does look nice, but
too much work. With Affinity, all I have to do is make it there, import to Spriter, and then import it into RPG Maker. This should cut my animation time by a significant amount.
You can get a low-cost Wacom pad for drawing between about $40 and $150 on Amazon or eBay. I like the hand-drawn look on many games. A game I used to quite enjoy was Draw a Stickman: EPIC. It is a rather simple stickman figure.
Similarly, Lisa and Omari used hand drawn with RPG Maker. They were a couple of the best-selling games from the engine. I'm good, but I'm not Davinci or Rockwell. Affinity should help me get a little bit closer to it.
There are guide tools with lock options for pen/paint directions. If you have an unsteady hand, it can correct it. Grid systems for making it as realistic as you want. If you want to use a tracing image for an artboard, there is a feature. When I do it in Illustrator, I had to go back and forth. If you use reference models from ArtStation or stock models, this could be a game-changer. A good example is turning models into anime characters.
Overall, using Affinity has significantly shortened my workflow and became my go-to app for design.
To me, it is the best alternative to Photoshop
. I still have a soft spot for Krita after using it for nearly 5 years, but it doesn't do vectors like I want on some pieces. Some customers can complain about image integrity and degrading, so keeping beautiful images for a long time is important to me.
Update: I found the image trace function with vectors. Wow. It will trace the image into a vector then I can export it back to raster. Little touch ups here and there, but massive amount of time savings!

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
I think this is the right move, but I wouldn't count on this being for forever. How long it will remain free, I'm not sure. 1 year? 2 years? 5 years? No one knows, but I see this as them likely making a strategic play to pull people away from the Adobe suite. It's a lot easier to say "I'll give it a try" when it's free. But it is still being published by a for-profit company, so they are likely deliberately taking a loss on this to earn marketshare, which is why I believe this isn't permanent and one day, will eventually return to, add a new, or change Affinity's revenue stream.
So... I say people should pick it up now even if they don't have plans to use it, lol
